tools.name: get_impact_report
tools.title: Get a TIA impact report
tools.description: The full Change Impact Report of one analysis (findings, evidence, test scope, policy outcomes, unknowns), as the caller may see it.

tools.name: find_impact_report
tools.title: Find the latest TIA report for a pull request or revision
tools.description: The newest report for a repository's pull request number or revision (commit id or prefix of 7+ characters).

tools.name: get_test_scope
tools.title: What to test for an analysis
tools.description: Which written test cases to regression-test and why, entry points to test, configuration and environment-variable checks, rule gaps, consistency checks, recommended tests and test gaps of one analysis.

tools.name: get_policy_outcome
tools.title: Release-policy outcome of an analysis
tools.description: Each configured release-policy rule's outcome (pass, fail, not_evaluated, requires_review) with its evidence, including approvals recorded since.

tools.name: get_tester_pack
tools.title: Tester pack of one change
tools.description: For the entry points one analysed change reaches: what to retest with a coverage gate (covered / gaps / not_evaluated), the UI locator pack of the pages that call them, and the API test matrix of the touched endpoints. 'Covered' means a test addresses the aspect, not that it passes.

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.title: Technical coverage of the test repository
tools.description: With no change: the technical aspects every entry point and page should be tested for (inputs, rules, error answers) and the automated tests and written test cases that address each: covered, partial or missing.

repositories.description: Optional: comma-separated repository names to limit the answer to.

tools.name: get_api_inventory
tools.title: API automation inventory
tools.description: Every endpoint with its inputs (mandatory, type, rules), generated valid and invalid values, a test matrix with expected outcomes and the error statuses its handler answers with.

repositories.description: Optional: comma-separated repository names to limit the answer to.

tools.name: get_ui_inventory
tools.title: UI automation inventory
tools.description: Every page with its elements: a locator for each (CSS, XPath, Playwright; fragile ones flagged), mandatory flags, input rules, dropdown values, and the API calls the page makes.

repositories.description: Optional: comma-separated repository names to limit the answer to.

tools.name: check_test_case
tools.title: Is this test case enough?
tools.description: One test case as a query: the entry points it addresses, the technical aspects it covers and the ones it misses. Matching is static and textual.

repositories.description: Optional: comma-separated repository names to limit the answer to.

tools.name: get_shared_components
tools.title: Shared components and rule gaps
tools.description: Endpoints and functions that several entry points depend on (a change to them needs the widest testing), and rules one consumer of a shared endpoint applies and another does not.

tools.name: query_graph
tools.title: Ask the code graph
tools.description: A direct question about one component, with no change involved. question: 'consumers' (who depends on it), 'dependencies' (what it depends on), 'tests' (which tests exercise it) or 'covers' (what one test exercises). component: a node id, 'METHOD /path', or a function, test, service, table or topic name. status is ok, ambiguous (candidates listed: ask again with one node id) or not_found. Always report the answer's 'limits'.

tools.name: get_business_impact
tools.title: Business impact of an analysis (Knowledge Fabric)
tools.description: The business side of a change, when the tenant's Knowledge Fabric bridge is on: the products (domain > product line) the change reaches, the Knowledge Fabric Systems the affected services realise, the requirements, processes, defects and incidents on them, and the business test cases covering those requirements, each with its chain from the code and its evidence status. Knowledge Fabric's own relationships come from its documents and are not verified by TIA: say so when you report them.

relationship_types.name: RETURNS

relationship_types.name: HAS_FIELD

relationship_types.name: HAS_EXAMPLE

relationship_types.name: APPLIES_RULE
relationship_types.description: The function applies the business rule.

relationship_types.name: COVERS
relationship_types.description: A written test case tests the endpoint or screen it names (Neo4j mirror only).

relationship_types.name: IMPACTS

bridge.name: tia-kf-bridge
bridge.description: The only relationships between TIA's software graph and Knowledge Fabric's business graph. Always from a TIA node to a Knowledge Fabric node, confined to one Knowledge Fabric customer; carry bridge=true, owner=tia, the evidence status and both sides' versions.

relationship_types.name: REALIZES
relationship_types.decided_by: declared alias (tenant setting knowledge_fabric.system_aliases, or business_systems in tia-services.yaml); otherwise the exact Knowledge Fabric key of the service or repository name
relationship_types.description: The service's code realises the named system (ArchiMate realization: an application component realises a business-facing system).

relationship_types.name: SAME_AS
relationship_types.decided_by: the same test case id under Knowledge Fabric's normalisation
relationship_types.description: The written test case in a repository and the Knowledge Fabric test case are the same test case.

relationship_types.name: REALIZES
relationship_types.decided_by: declared alias (knowledge_fabric.screen_aliases by route or component, or business_screens in tia-services.yaml); otherwise the exact Knowledge Fabric key of the component or of the route's last segment
relationship_types.description: The screen realises the form or screen the documents describe.

relationship_types.name: STORES
relationship_types.decided_by: declared alias (knowledge_fabric.data_aliases, or business_data in tia-services.yaml); otherwise the exact key of the class name, or of the class name without a technical suffix (Record, Entity, Model, Dto, View, Row)
relationship_types.description: The ORM entity stores the business data entity.

relationship_types.name: STORES
relationship_types.decided_by: declared alias; otherwise the exact key of the table name or of its singular
relationship_types.description: The table stores the business data entity.

relationship_types.name: ENFORCES
relationship_types.decided_by: a person confirms a pair TIA proposed (shared field names, then word overlap); rule names are sentences, so names alone never link
relationship_types.description: The rule found in code enforces the business rule.

relationship_types.name: PLACED_IN
relationship_types.decided_by: a person: tenant setting knowledge_fabric.repository_products / service_products, business_products in tia-services.yaml, or a reviewer accepting a suggestion (a suggestion from the linked Systems is never applied by itself)
relationship_types.description: The service belongs to this ProductLine of the customer's business tree (domain > product line > function > sub-function); every impact of the service rolls up the tree from here. Carries product_line_id, because one function can sit under two product lines.

relationship_types.description: The service belongs to this Function of the customer's business tree (domain > product line > function > sub-function); every impact of the service rolls up the tree from here. Carries product_line_id, because one function can sit under two product lines.

relationship_types.description: The service belongs to this SubFunction of the customer's business tree (domain > product line > function > sub-function); every impact of the service rolls up the tree from here. Carries product_line_id, because one function can sit under two product lines.

relationship_types.name: IMPLEMENTS_CHANGE
relationship_types.decided_by: an issue key (PAY-4521) in a commit message of the change that Knowledge Fabric keeps as the user story's name or alias
relationship_types.description: The change implements the user story. Reported in the analysis (business_impact.user_stories), not stored in Neo4j: a change is an analysis, not a node of the mirror.
